how: The opening speaker proposes an MU logo and calls fellow Tigers to help make it.
Recruitment ranges from representing the university to requesting five to ten people for twenty minutes of defence.
Participants revise lettering and compare border designs while fitting the image to neighbouring work and available hands.
Participants report a MIZ begun at specified coordinates and distinguish the state of its letters during defence.
A logo reference, numerical coordinates and landmarks make the proposed work locatable without establishing a pixel template.
Defenders join an uphill fight, encourage each other and stop for sleep while hoping the image survives.
The candidate attribution process appears as participants assigning blue pixels and attempted letter conversion to named rivals.
A direct reply restrains proposed flag encroachment by recommending a smaller border because the group cannot compete or maintain expansion.
The secret proposal to replace one row of a neighbour's flag makes encroachment part of building a defensible border.
The element's fresh-start range fits rebuilding the same lost spot and considering downward extension without demonstrating relocation.
Crediting the people who took and defended a temporary position remains possible after the room reports having no final spot.
Participants mark the ending, report the failed final presence and preserve a modest screenshot taken before sleep.
The white-border proposal receives an unqualified yes from another participant.
An explicit shortage of people constrains simultaneous maintenance and expansion.
The candidate's existing-body range appears narrowly when fellow Tigers are called to represent themselves through the university logo.
Participants mock the rival's scrambled image and invite others to enjoy its reported frustration.
The existing letters become objects of defence while construction remains unfinished, fitting the model’s range of repair and upkeep.
Design coordination can proceed through an early reference and later verbal revisions without a subsequently posted pixel template settling the design.
A proposal receives a bare affirmative answer, supporting this local response pattern without establishing obligations on silent readers.
A proposed encroachment receives a direct counterproposal that gives competition and insufficient maintenance labour as reasons to pull back.
Too few hands can elicit a smaller border and continued same-site recovery rather than requiring withdrawal and relocation.
Credit and pride can mark temporary collective defence after loss, without a completed surviving work as their prerequisite.
Distinguish reconstructing an image reported gone from repairing still-standing pixels and recruit help for that renewed effort.
Continued recovery depends on members' available attention, which meetings and screen-sharing can interrupt even when they remain willing to help.
Temporary success holding opponents off must remain distinguishable from victory through final survival when the speaker expressly reports no final spot.
Keep attribution at the speaker's stated certainty when the account assumes responsibility or reports an apparent rival move without independently tracing placers.
A deleted plan and an informal design preference cannot decide hidden governance or test the comparative claim about most rooms.
Rival nicknames and retrospective credit for taking a spot do not independently establish that an earlier school tie motivated the original attack.
The event concepts show rivalry but do not independently date the quarrel before the canvas.
The visible logo call and labour reports do not document a separate host-sub April Fools framing.
Internal border proposals do not document a neighbour's agreement, and the hinted diversion of rivals supplies no negotiated terms.
Scarcity and interrupted placing are documented without establishing whether automation was used elsewhere.
Calls address the room's defenders without documenting requests to other rooms or traded help.
A proposed spot beside other colleges does not establish coalition membership or a joint defence agreement.
Using a flag as a proposed edge does not document a host's permission or rule over a guest work.

Without a documented inter-room agreement, questions about the drawing plan cannot test a dispute over who binds placers.
Sharing a pre-sleep screenshot records an attempt without documenting a dispute over cleanup or the historical version retained.
A build report follows recruitment but does not explicitly attribute the participant's action to the call.
The starter proposes and recruits in the same passage, leaving a separate start-to-call transition unestablished.
Defence and internal border planning are visible without a documented turn to negotiation with neighbours.

Reported maintenance strain does not document a subsequent turn to scripts or spare accounts.
Credit and screenshot preservation coexist without a passage linking celebration causally to the decision to record.

Calls for help under attack do not document an ensuing appeal to other rooms or help sent by them.
Internal border discussion supplies neither an inter-room negotiating channel nor a subsequent exchange of help.
An initial call and later encroachment proposal establish sequence without showing that recruitment caused a turn against rival work.
The direct answer to proposed encroachment scales the design to labour rather than documenting a truce or negotiated deal.
Mockery accompanies the contest without establishing that a particular attack caused the subsequent rival-directed talk.
Pressure on defenders is documented without an ensuing coalition or mutual defence arrangement.
Visible recruitment does not document the claimed flood or a response containing canvas talk.
